text: Heavy rain disrupted suburban train services in Mumbai on Monday, according to Central Railway. Commuters at Dadar and Kurla waited for hours as water covered the tracks near the platforms. Railway spokesperson Anita Deshmukh said crews from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation were pumping out the flooded sections. Services are expected to return to normal by Tuesday morning, she added.

Jordan Paris, a former analyst at Goldman Sachs, joined the board of Infosys on Tuesday. Paris, who grew up in Lyon, said he wanted to help the company expand its operations across Europe over the next three years. Chairman Nandan Rao welcomed the appointment and described the new director as a careful and patient listener.

Washington has asked Beijing to explain the sudden export restrictions on rare minerals. A US trade official, Linda Washington, said talks would continue in Geneva next week and that no final decision had been made. The World Trade Organization was not involved in the discussions, she said, though it had been informed.

Apple opened a new retail store in Bengaluru on Saturday, drawing large crowds from across Karnataka. Store manager Priya Nair said the opening had been planned for many months. Local farmers, meanwhile, complained that the price of apples had dropped sharply at the nearby wholesale market because of a bumper harvest.

The WHO said it would send medical teams to Kenya after floods displaced thousands of families. Dr. Amina Yusuf, who coordinates the response, said the people who need help most live near Lake Victoria. Officials asked anyone who can donate to contact the Red Cross, and said who receives the supplies first will depend on road access.

Victoria Clarke, a spokesperson for Victoria Police, confirmed on Wednesday that officers had arrested two men in Melbourne. The suspects were taken to a station in St. Kilda for questioning. Clarke declined to name them and said the investigation was at an early stage.

Shares of Tata Motors rose 3 percent after the company reported strong sales in the UK. Analysts at Morgan Stanley said the Jaguar Land Rover unit had performed better than expected this quarter. Chief executive Rohit Menon said demand across Asia remained steady, though he warned that supply of semiconductors could stay tight.

In the final on Sunday, Georgia Hughes beat compatriot Chelsea Brown in straight sets. Hughes, who now lives in Georgia, thanked her coach and the fans in London after the match. The tournament was played at the All England Club, where rain delayed the start by nearly two hours.

Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science published a study on groundwater levels in Rajasthan. Lead author Dr. Meera Iyer said the data came from NASA satellites and from local wells monitored over ten years. The study was funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and will be presented at a conference next spring.

Amazon announced plans to hire 5,000 workers in Hyderabad this year, spokesperson Neha Kapoor said. In an unrelated report, Greenpeace warned that deforestation in the Amazon had reached a record high. Kapoor did not comment on the report, and the company said its hiring plans were unaffected by it.

Mercury Capital, a fund based in Singapore, named Hassan Al-Rashid as its new head of operations. Al-Rashid previously worked at HSBC in Dubai and later at the Reserve Bank of India. He said the fund would keep its focus on long-term investments rather than quick trades.

The Lincoln Center will host a concert by the Mumbai Symphony Orchestra next month. Conductor Lincoln Sharma, who was born in Pune, said the program would include works by Mozart and a new piece by a young composer from Kochi. Tickets will go on sale on Friday.

Acme Robotics Inc. said on Friday that its CEO, Martin Cole Jr., would visit Mt. Abu and St. Petersburg to meet suppliers. The visit follows a supply deal with Siemens AG, a German engineering group. The agreement is worth several million dollars, according to people familiar with the matter.

IT firms in Noida and Chennai reported a rise in hiring, according to Nasscom. The Times of India said Wipro and Cognizant were among the companies expanding their teams. Most of the new jobs are in artificial intelligence, a field where demand for skilled engineers continues to outpace supply.

May Fernandes, a lawyer at Khaitan & Co, said the ruling would take effect in May. The Supreme Court of India had earlier dismissed an appeal filed by Reliance Industries, bringing a long dispute to an end. Fernandes said her clients were relieved but cautious about what comes next.

Sky News reported that Brooklyn Adams, a striker for Brighton, had left for Madrid after talks with Real Madrid. Adams said he was grateful to the fans, who had supported him through a difficult season. The club has not confirmed the transfer fee, but local media suggested it was substantial.

Cyclone warnings were issued for Odisha and West Bengal by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Thursday. The IMD said winds could reach 100 kilometres per hour along the coast. Officials in Bhubaneswar told fishermen to stay ashore and asked schools to remain closed until further notice.

Reuters said UN envoy Sofia Alvarez would meet political leaders in Nairobi on Thursday. The UN, which is based in New York, has called for urgent talks. Alvarez said the crisis affects all of us, not only the US, and urged governments to act together.
